title: Find the Non-Repeating Element
statement:
You are given an array of `n` integers in which every value appears **exactly twice**, except for one value that appears **exactly once**. Find and print that value.

The positions of the elements are arbitrary: equal values need not be adjacent and the array is not sorted. Note that `n` is always odd.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print the single value that appears only once.
constraints: Exactly one value appears once; every other value appears exactly twice.

examples.explanation: Values 1 and 2 each appear twice. Value 4 appears once.
-5, 3 and 9 are each paired up, leaving 8.
A single element is the one that does not repeat.

hints: A hash map of counts works in O(n) time and O(n) memory. Can you do it with O(1) memory?
What happens when you XOR a number with itself? And with 0?
XOR all the elements together: paired values cancel to 0, and the lone value remains.
